newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Eddington appointed Ansett executive chairman.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Eddington appointed Ansett executive chairman.

text.p: News Corp Ltd unit News Ltd said on Friday that current Cathay Pacific Ltd Managing Director Rod Eddington would be appointed as executive chairman of Ansett Australia.
The appointment had the full support of Air New Zealand Ltd, which has agreed to buy TNT Ltd's 50 percent stake in Ansett, News Ltd said. News owns the other 50 percent of Ansett.
Current Ansett executive chairman Ken Cowley said he would retain a role at Ansett Australia as a director.
Cowley, who is also News Ltd executive chairman, said in a statement Eddington would be appointed News Ltd's representative for aviation interests for Ansett Australia from January 1997.
"In this capacity, Mr Eddington will assume the role of Executive Chairman of Ansett Australia," Cowley said. "This appointment has the full support of Air New Zealand," he said.
An Ansett spokeswoman later Reuters that Eddington's appointment as Ansett Executive Chairman was also effective from January 1997.
"Rod's appointment marks the culmination of extensive negotiations, a lengthy and considered process befitting one of the industry's finest executives," Cowley said.
Eddington would report to Cowley, he said.
"I had always planned to relinquish my role as executive chairman once a suitably talented aviation manager was secured for News."
Cowley would assume the chairmanship of Ansett New Zealand, which is to be 100 percent owned by News, and would be News Ltd's nominee for board representative at Ansett International.
Eddington said in the same statement that Ansett Australia faced an exciting period with the welcoming of a new partner in Air New Zealand.
"Together we will create new synergies and additional opportunities for growth," he said.

"And I look forward to working with the Ansett Australia team in the confidence we will achieve our goals: to increase revenues, reduce costs and retain the enviable reputation for high safety standards and customer service of which Ansett is so justifiably proud."

Cowley said last month Ansett had to cut A$150 million from Ansett's annual cost base of A$3 billion over the next two years. He also aaid Ansett wanted to raise revenues by about the same amount over that time.

TNT Ltd announced earlier this month it would sell its 50 percent stake to Air New Zealand for a total investment of A$475 million, including A$325 million in payments to TNT and A$150 million in investment into Ansett.
News also agreed to invest another A$50 million in the troubled airline, which is estimated to have made a small loss in the year to June 30, 1995.
Under the deal, Ansett will also sell 51 percent of its international airline business to a new company owned by Australian institutional investors to meet foreign ownership requirements.
Also News takes 100 percent control of Ansett New Zealand, Air New Zealand's main domestic competitor, to satisfy the concerns of New Zealand's anti-monopoly regulator.
Earlier on Friday Air New Zealand's shareholders approved the purchase.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
